macro.narrative: The expansionary ISM manufacturing and services data, coupled with a steepening yield curve and low VIX, signal robust end‑market demand for sales‑enablement tools. ZoomInfo’s growing upmarket ACV mix and subscription‑based model give it pricing power, while the favorable financing environment supports its planned AI‑platform capex. The macro backdrop also encourages competitors to expand, potentially tightening pricing pressure, but the company’s focus on higher‑margin enterprise customers mitigates this risk.

implications.why: Higher ISM new orders and PMI indicate stronger corporate spending on sales tools, boosting ZoomInfo’s revenue growth.
Upmarket ACV mix and subscription model allow ZoomInfo to maintain margins despite competitive pricing pressure.
Low financing costs and an upward‑sloping yield curve support investment in AI‑platform development, potentially driving future revenue.
The yield curve remains steep but rates are still low, keeping debt servicing costs manageable for ZoomInfo.
Improved cash flow from higher revenue and efficient collections strengthens working capital and supports growth initiatives.
